statement: New, and ours. gate.concern_of returned the probe's prose for coverage and scale unconditionally whenever the state was `measured`, never reading the finding's own ok/fail. The branch was written when coverage could never read anything -- it refused without a patches.json the core desk never wrote -- so it was dead code and its unconditional return was invisible. export_patches writes that manifest, so this is the first sweep in which coverage could measure, and it warned on 19 of the 20 runs that measured it, every one an exhaustive and disjoint partition. Eighteen desks spent a declare turn waiving it; T12's only declare landed on turn 30 of 30 and was bounced for want of a waiver it had no turn left to give.

statement: New, and ours. The brief says a cell that outruns its window is 'reported back as still running ... and your next step either polls it or interrupts it on purpose'. The desk's only action is run_cell, and any cell it sends queues behind the running one for a full window while the harness's automatic poll adds nothing. T15, correctly told its cell was still running, sent print('poll: ...') and then print('poll export') -- 480 s of a 900 s budget for two lines that told it nothing.

statement: WITHDRAWN on re-vet, 2026-09-17. This graded a route the request explicitly disclaims: T4 says 'Mesh the water side only', and building the water volume directly as a union of channel boxes satisfies every word of it. The demand for a subtraction comes from the case file's `## What this catches` section, which is a provenance note citing plan section 2 about OCCT's thin-wall boolean -- the harness's interest, not the requester's. T4's three named properties say nothing about the aluminium block, and the desk satisfied two of them. What it actually failed to do is print the minimum local width, which is named_requirement_dropped_without_mention and is already filed. If we want the boolean exercised, the request has to ask for it.

checkMesh Total volume = 3.5993135e-06 against the desk's own CAD 3599.823 mm^3 -- the water side, correct and beside the point

statement: Recurs on 4 of 26 -- and on re-vet the geometry holds in all four, which makes this the measurement failure and not a false pass. T9's clearance is spanned by 2 cells and T19's by 4, both measured by the vet on constant/polyMesh; T23's volume is within 0.2% of a 20M-sample Monte Carlo integration; T26's tread is built from the shaft axis and fused with the column, which puts the excess inside the column where it is subtracted away, so the delivered wetted surface is what a tangent tread would give, with the zero-area contact removed, and the desk said so. In none of the four does the run's own record establish any of this. The id's name imports the case file's 'A pass that is really a failure' section as a criterion; it is a design note about why the case exists, not an acceptance test.
